newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mostly higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open mostly higher Friday, led by overnight gains in platinum and palladium, after a threat of a strike at South Africa's Implats platinum refineries.
COMEX December gold was called unchanged to up $0.50 from Thursday's close of $328.60 an ounce, although a further rise in the dollar is expected to cap any gold rally.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $325.30/60 early compared to the London morning fix of $325.30 and the New York close Thursday of $324.30/80.

COMEX warehouse gold stocks fell just 64 ounces to 914,011 ounces Thursday, while COMEX silver stocks fell a further 1,291,545 ounces to 169,609,413 ounces, the lowest level since the addition of the Wilmington Trust stocks in January.
COMEX September silver was called unchanged to down 1.0 cent from Thursday's finish of $4.49 after an upside breakout of a three-week-old range between $4.20 and $4.40.

NYMEX October platinum was called up $1.00 to $2.00 from the previous close of $425.50 after the contract hit a new life-of-contract high of $434.00. NYMEX September palladium was called up $3.00 to $5.00 from Thursday's close of $200.60 after also climbing a contract peak.

PGM futures surged even higher on TOCOM overnight for the third straight session as shortcovering continued, with spot market sales of platinum-group metals by Russia not meeting pent-up demand, traders said.

Meanwhile, South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats) said Friday all workers at its platinum refineries had reported for work desite the National Union of Mineworkers notice of a strike on Thursday.
